outcome: Occurrence of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) in relation to parity
cohort: The study participants were 56 women who developed postpartum hemorrhage after a Cesarean section and had a compression B-Lynch suture applied in a clinic in Lodz, Poland.
finding: The B-Lynch suture was effective in 92.86% of cases for uterine atony, significantly reducing the frequency of radical procedures like hysterectomy in women experiencing PPH after Cesarean section.
